A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REA-RL research despite the shortened title in v2. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original math-reasoning experiments, including accuracy and token consumption, reflection-model comparisons, reward ablations, and post-training overthinking analyses in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains original math experiments and adds evaluated baselines, general-QA and smaller-model results, heuristic-truncation comparisons, and measured token consumption and latency.

M1.justification: The GRPO procedure, learned overthinking detector, sequential revision, response filtering, and length/reflection rewards remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 applies the existing procedure with different model sizes and training data; it does not introduce a new algorithmic component. The all-incorrect-group filtering rule moves to Appendix B.2.

E1.justification: v2 removes OlympiadBench from the evaluated math suite, retaining the other five benchmarks and DeepScaleR training data. Appendix B.3 adds training and evaluation on MMLU, MMLU-Pro, and SuperGPQA, substantially extending coverage from mathematical problem solving to general multiple-choice QA.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds evaluated NoThink, ShorterBetter, Light-R1, DAST, and Arora–Zanette baselines. Table 3 adds untrained Qwen-7B revision with and without gold answers; v1's trained '7B Revise' rows instead correspond to v2's MReflect rows. Table 9 adds first- and fifth-reflection heuristic truncation baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 introduces 1.5B policy and 4B reflection-model configurations, a mixed QA training set, shortest-path filtering, 5,000 test examples per QA dataset, and one generated path per test question. The reported main training budget also changes from 1,800 steps to one epoch with matched steps for other methods; this does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds untrained-detector comparisons, heuristic-cutoff tests, reflection-model size comparisons on QA, and token/latency analysis. Figure 3 replaces GSM8K-only training dynamics with averages over five test sets. The reward/quantile ablations and post-training overthinking analysis already existed in v1 and move to Appendices B.4 and B.6.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without confidence intervals, significance tests, or independent training-run and seed counts. Sampling eight paths per AMC23/AIME24 question is retained. The new QA sampling protocol does not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds baseline, QA, smaller-model, heuristic, and cost results while removing Olympiad entries. Shared methods' per-dataset math scores remain unchanged. For example, the combined method's 16k average accuracy/token ratio changes from 77.13/65.11 to 80.74/63.51 because the average now excludes Olympiad, not because performance improved under the same benchmark coverage.

T1.justification: The advantage decomposition and reward definitions are mathematically unchanged. v2 makes GRPO normalization explicit and writes the previously described refined length reward as Equation 4. Renaming 'partial reward' to 'partial advantage' clarifies terminology without changing the derivation; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion update the headline token savings from 35% to 36%, consistent with the revised benchmark average. The central contributions—online sequential revision and reflection-aware rewards that reduce reasoning length while preserving performance—remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 changes the explanation of the component trade-off from overlapping encouragement of reflection to tension between penalizing overthinking and encouraging reflection. New appendix discussions interpret transfer across domains/model sizes, explain why reflection-token heuristics truncate useful reasoning, and distinguish local latency overhead from potential large-scale token-cost savings.

D1.justification: v2 adds checkpoint/prompt sourcing for new baselines, the NoThink prompt, QA data-construction and generation details, and per-batch token and timing measurements. Its reproducibility statement explicitly includes configuration files and evaluation scripts at the existing repository. Most core hyperparameters, prompts, hardware, and total training times were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations for NoThink, ShorterBetter, Light-R1, DeepCompress, QA benchmarks, and data filtering/synthesis work, while removing the general LRM-background paragraph. The main positioning against offline response revision and online length-reward methods remains intact. Publication and citation-style updates do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative and much of the prose are retained. v2 edits related work and method explanations, moves dataset descriptions to Section 5.1 and common training settings to Appendix B.2, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements. The title, affiliations, and reward/advantage terminology also change.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to distinguish shared advantages from partial penalties/rewards, and Figure 3 changes its plotted summaries and scales. Tables gain baseline rows, lose the Olympiad column, and change highlighting conventions; four new tables present additional experiments. The conference template also changes typography, headers, and placement throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged method through relevant additional competitors, detector and heuristic comparisons, and experiments beyond a single 7B math policy. These address important comparative and generality gaps in v1; the measured cost breakdown also clarifies the known training overhead. The improvement concerns evidential support, not higher same-setting performance. Tradeoffs remain: Olympiad coverage is removed, uncertainty reporting is still absent, and the conclusion's retained claim of validation only on 7B models conflicts with the new 1.5B experiments.
